job.style: a market or shop situation that uses the idea

response.passage: Rohan visited the local village market to buy materials for his school project. He first looked at two rectangular wooden boards. The first board measured 4 meters by 2 meters, while the second board was 5 meters by 1 meter. Rohan noticed that both boards had a perimeter of 12 meters, but they covered different amounts of space. He realized that having the same boundary length does not mean the shapes enclose the same amount of surface area. Next, he went to a tile shop to buy square tiles for his floor. The shopkeeper explained that one square meter is equal to 10,000 square centimeters. Rohan was surprised because he initially thought it was only 100 square centimeters. He carefully calculated the area of his room to ensure he bought enough tiles. He also bought a circular mat with a circumference of 62.8 centimeters. He learned that the area of a shape is measured in square units, while the perimeter is measured in linear units. By understanding these differences, Rohan successfully completed his project without wasting any money or materials. He felt confident applying these mathematical concepts to real-life situations at the market.
response.summary: Rohan learns that shapes with equal perimeters can have different areas. He also discovers the correct conversion between square meters and square centimeters while shopping for his project.
